model_fitness.best_available_model: Two-tier: (1) Mecp2-heterozygous female mouse neurons/organotypic slices or primary cortical cultures carrying an allele-distinguishable Mecp2 (X-linked GFP or strain-polymorphic reporter) for single-cell allelic readout; (2) Mecp2+/- female mice dosed ICV/intrathecally with Xist-targeting RNase-H ASO alone. Human-cell arm: patient-derived fibroblasts/iPSC neurons with H3K9/H4K16 hyperacetylation as rescue readout (EVIDENCE, PMID 35460749). The published Xi-reactivation proof used genetic Xist ablation plus 5-aza-dC, not an ASO-only regimen (EVIDENCE contradictory, PMID 29282321).
model_fitness.captures_relevant_mechanism: Partially. Mosaic X-inactivation, the endogenous silenced wild-type MECP2 allele and native-promoter dose capping are all faithfully present in Mecp2+/- female mice (EVIDENCE, PMID 40673967). What is NOT captured is whether ASO-only Xist knockdown suffices in vivo: the only in vivo reactivation evidence required genetic Xist loss plus a DNMT inhibitor (EVIDENCE, PMID 29282321), so the model can test the drug-like hypothesis but has never been shown to support it.
model_fitness.captures_relevant_cell_type: Yes for cortex/hippocampus, weakly for brainstem. ASOs delivered ICV/IT reach cortical and hippocampal neurons and glia; brainstem respiratory nuclei are the dominant morbidity driver and the least well exposed, and mouse CSF geometry systematically overstates deep-structure exposure relative to human brain (INFERENCE from nusinersen/tofersen precedent and PMID 26605526).
model_fitness.measurable_phenotype: Quantitative and decision-grade at the cell level: fraction of individual neurons switching to wild-type-allele MECP2 expression (allele-specific single-cell/single-nucleus RNA-seq or allelic MeCP2 immunostaining), chromosome-wide X-linked reactivation breadth in the same cells, Xist knockdown magnitude, plus regional mapping (cortex vs hippocampus vs brainstem). Secondary: H3K9/H4K16 acetylation normalisation (EVIDENCE, PMID 35460749).
model_fitness.important_limitations: Mouse behavioural endpoints are unreliable proxies here: environmental enrichment normalised rotarod/open-field in Mecp2+/- mice while prefrontal/anterior cingulate projection abnormalities persisted (EVIDENCE contradictory, PMID 40673967), so behaviour must not be the primary readout. Mouse-to-human IT biodistribution scaling is the single biggest extrapolation gap. Xist sequence and X-inactivation maintenance differ between mouse and human, so an ASO validated in mouse is not the clinical candidate.

plan.critical_question: Can an ASO alone (no DNA-methyltransferase inhibitor) flip a large fraction of individual MeCP2-null neurons to wild-type MECP2 expression in vivo at tolerable CNS doses — and does it do so without chromosome-wide X-linked gene reactivation? This is the one unknown that gates the entire strategy; everything downstream is moot if the per-cell switch rate is low.
plan.proposed_experiment: Single, cell-resolution dose-ranging study. Dose Mecp2+/- female mice (allele-distinguishable Mecp2, symptomatic age) with a Xist RNase-H ASO by ICV bolus across 3-4 doses, ASO-alone arms plus a positive-control arm with short-course 5-aza-dC to anchor the achievable ceiling, and scramble-ASO controls. After 2 and 6 weeks, microdissect cortex, hippocampus and brainstem and run (a) Xist RT-qPCR for target engagement, (b) allele-specific single-nucleus RNA-seq to score, per neuron, whether the wild-type MECP2 allele is expressed, (c) the same snRNA-seq data to quantify how many other X-linked genes are reactivated in those cells, (d) MeCP2 immunostaining to confirm protein-level, nuclear restoration. Pre-specify the primary endpoint as percent of neurons converted per region, not any behavioural measure. Run the human-cell counterpart in parallel: patient iPSC-derived neurons with human XIST ASOs, scoring allelic MECP2 and H3K9/H4K16 acetylation reversal (EVIDENCE basis, PMID 35460749).
plan.model: Symptomatic Mecp2+/- female mice with allele-distinguishable Mecp2 expression, ICV/intrathecal ASO dosing; parallel patient-derived iPSC neurons for human XIST pharmacology.
plan.primary_readout: Percent of MeCP2-null neurons converted to wild-type MECP2 expression, by region (cortex, hippocampus, brainstem), with the number of co-reactivated X-linked genes per converted cell as the paired safety readout.
plan.supportive_result: ASO alone converts a substantial fraction of null neurons (pre-specify >=25-30%) in at least cortex and hippocampus, with measurable brainstem conversion, nuclear MeCP2 protein restored, and reactivation largely confined to a small number of X-linked loci rather than chromosome-wide. Decision: the drug-like version of the strategy exists; advance to human XIST ASO screening and a brainstem-weighted delivery optimisation campaign, and only then look at behaviour/survival.
plan.negative_result: ASO alone achieves strong Xist knockdown but few percent neuronal conversion, or conversion only in superficial cortex with none in brainstem, or conversion is inseparable from broad chromosome-wide X reactivation, or conversion requires the DNMT inhibitor. Decision: stop the Xi-reactivation ASO program as a standalone therapeutic. A result where conversion depends on 5-aza-dC specifically converts this into an epigenetic-reprogramming safety problem rather than an oligonucleotide problem, and should be deprioritised rather than reformulated.
plan.decision_enabled: Whether to invest in an Xi-reactivation oligonucleotide program at all. This experiment is deliberately designed to kill the approach cheaply: it tests the per-cell switch rate — the assumption on which everything rests — before any money goes into human-sequence chemistry, brainstem delivery engineering or behavioural efficacy studies. It also replaces the misleading endpoint (rodent behaviour, shown dissociable from circuit correction, PMID 40673967) with a mechanistic one. Note the strategy's splice-switching sub-route (patients with splice-site/pseudoexon MECP2 variants) is a separate, much more conventional decision and should be assessed on stratum size first, not with this experiment.

model_fitness.best_available_model: Mecp2-/y male mice (the model in which TAT-MeCP2 extended lifespan >50% with CA2 soma-size rescue; EVIDENCE, PMID 35460749) for efficacy, but Mecp2+/- female mice for the question that actually matters here, because only the female mosaic contains the wild-type-expressing neurons at risk of overdose. Human-cell arm: patient fibroblasts with H3K9/H4K16 hyperacetylation reversal as an on-target potency assay (EVIDENCE, PMID 35460749).
model_fitness.captures_relevant_mechanism: Mechanism of action yes, therapeutic window no. The null male model demonstrates that supplying MeCP2 protein is functionally therapeutic (EVIDENCE, PMID 35460749) but it structurally cannot reveal the dominant risk, because it has no wild-type-expressing cells to overdose. The bidirectional dose constraint is established independently (duplication syndrome; ASO lowering rescues duplication mice; EVIDENCE, PMID 26605526). MeCP2 is an entirely nuclear chromosomal methyl-CpG-binding protein with no extracellular site of action (EVIDENCE, UniProt P51608), so three serial barriers (BBB, plasma membrane, nuclear import) are intrinsic to the mechanism and are the least well modelled aspect.
model_fitness.captures_relevant_cell_type: Partially. Published evidence establishes functional rescue in hippocampal CA2 but the fraction of neurons achieving nuclear MeCP2 occupancy was never established as a delivery parameter (INFERENCE from PMID 35460749), and brainstem respiratory nuclei — the mortality driver — were not characterised. TAT-mediated uptake is non-selective and dominated by peripheral organs (INFERENCE).
model_fitness.measurable_phenotype: The decision-relevant phenotype is measurable but has not been measured: per-cell, per-cell-type nuclear MeCP2 occupancy quantified against the endogenous wild-type level, scored separately in mutant-expressing and wild-type-expressing neurons of a mosaic female. Readouts exist (quantitative nuclear immunofluorescence with allelic reporter, H3K9/H4K16 acetylation).
model_fitness.important_limitations: Mouse brain is ~1/1000 the volume of human brain with a correspondingly shorter diffusion path, so murine brain exposure of a 486-aa fusion protein does not scale (INFERENCE, PMID 35460749). Lifespan and behaviour in Mecp2-/y males are the endpoints most likely to overstate translatable benefit, given demonstrated behaviour/circuit dissociation in Mecp2+/- mice (EVIDENCE contradictory, PMID 40673967). Chronic immunogenicity of a viral-TAT-fused nuclear antigen is not assessable in short rodent studies (INFERENCE). No MeCP2 protein therapeutic has reached the clinic despite mouse data since 2022 (EVIDENCE, ClinicalTrials.gov Rett syndrome search).

plan.critical_question: In a mosaic female brain, is there any dose of cell-penetrating MeCP2 protein that puts near-physiological MeCP2 into the nuclei of a large fraction of null neurons without pushing co-resident wild-type-expressing neurons into the duplication-syndrome range? Equivalently: does a therapeutic window exist at all, measured per cell rather than per animal?
plan.proposed_experiment: Window-mapping, not efficacy. Dose symptomatic Mecp2+/- female mice (allele-distinguishable, so wild-type- and mutant-expressing neurons can be told apart in situ) with TAT-MeCP2e2 across a 4-5 point dose range including the published efficacious dose, plus vehicle. At peak exposure and trough, quantify by calibrated single-cell nuclear immunofluorescence, in cortex, hippocampal CA2 and brainstem respiratory nuclei separately: (i) the fraction of mutant-expressing neurons reaching >=50% of normal nuclear MeCP2, and (ii) the distribution of total nuclear MeCP2 in wild-type-expressing neurons expressed as fold-over-endogenous. Plot the two curves against dose. Pair with H3K9/H4K16 acetylation in the same sections as a functional confirmation that nuclear protein is active, and run the patient-fibroblast acetylation assay to set the in vitro occupancy-to-activity calibration (EVIDENCE basis, PMID 35460749). Deliberately exclude survival and behavioural endpoints from this study.
plan.model: Symptomatic Mecp2+/- female mice with allele-distinguishable Mecp2 expression (mosaic architecture is mandatory); patient fibroblasts for occupancy-activity calibration.
plan.primary_readout: Two superimposed dose-response curves per brain region: fraction of null neurons achieving near-physiological nuclear MeCP2, versus fold-over-endogenous nuclear MeCP2 in wild-type-expressing neurons. The separation (or lack of it) between these curves is the answer.
plan.supportive_result: A dose range exists where a large fraction (>=50%) of null neurons reach near-physiological nuclear MeCP2 — including measurable brainstem coverage — while wild-type-expressing neurons stay below roughly 1.5-2x endogenous. Decision: the window is real; the remaining problem is engineering (BBB shuttle instead of TAT, human-scale biodistribution modelling, immunogenicity), and the program is worth funding past the delivery question.
plan.negative_result: The curves are inseparable — doses that load null neurons also push wild-type neurons well above endogenous — or the converted fraction remains low (single-digit to low-double-digit percent) at tolerated doses, or brainstem occupancy is near-zero at every dose. Decision: close the cell-penetrating MeCP2 protein route. The published lifespan extension would then be reinterpreted as a low-occupancy effect peculiar to the null male (which has no overdose ceiling), and any revival would require a genuinely cell-selective delivery concept, not dose optimisation.
plan.decision_enabled: Whether to fund MeCP2 protein replacement beyond the existing tool-compound stage. This experiment is the cheapest available test of the specific feature that makes this modality uniquely fragile — non-selective uptake into a mosaic tissue where half the cells must not be loaded. It uses the correct model (female mosaic, not null male), measures the correct variable (per-cell nuclear occupancy, never previously reported), and avoids the endpoint known to mislead in this disease (rodent behaviour; PMID 40673967). A negative result ends the program on mechanism rather than after years of protein engineering; a positive result reframes the work as a delivery-engineering problem with a defined target product profile.

model_fitness.best_available_model: No adequate model exists for the gating question, and no MECP2 mRNA/LNP work was retrievable (EVIDENCE, PubMed zero hits for MECP2 mRNA lipid nanoparticle delivery; no RNA therapeutic in the Rett clinical landscape, ClinicalTrials.gov). The nearest usable surrogate is a carrier-screening model that is MECP2-agnostic: ICV/intrathecal delivery of a reporter mRNA in wild-type mice with single-cell quantification of neuronal versus glial transfection by region. Human-cell counterpart: patient iPSC-derived neurons for per-cell MeCP2 output and the H3K9/H4K16 acetylation potency assay (EVIDENCE basis, PMID 35460749).
model_fitness.captures_relevant_mechanism: No, and that is the point. The therapeutic logic (supplying MeCP2 activity rescues null cells) is supported (EVIDENCE, PMID 35460749), but the modality's two fatal features — a transient uncontrolled per-cell protein burst into a bidirectionally dose-sensitive locus (EVIDENCE, PMID 26605526) and uptake that is blind to X-inactivation status in a mosaic — are not represented in any existing model because no carrier reaches the relevant cells. The decision therefore turns on carrier capability, which is a delivery question upstream of any MECP2-specific biology.
model_fitness.captures_relevant_cell_type: No. Intrathecal/ICV LNP in published rodent work gives patchy, largely ependymal, perivascular and glial transfection with weak deep-parenchymal neuronal uptake; the disease-driving population is deep, widely distributed postmitotic neurons including brainstem (INFERENCE). No carrier achieving near-pan-neuronal mRNA delivery across a human-sized brain is known.
model_fitness.measurable_phenotype: A carrier-screening phenotype is measurable (percent of neurons transfected, by region and cell class). A MECP2-specific therapeutic phenotype is not yet measurable in vivo because the prerequisite delivery does not exist.
model_fitness.important_limitations: Rodent CSF geometry flatters intrathecal delivery relative to human brain. Reporter mRNA overstates usable expression for a protein needing nuclear import and titrated levels. Repeat-dose innate reactogenicity and anti-PEG responses over a lifetime horizon are not addressable in short studies. Rodent behavioural rescue is dissociable from circuit correction and would flatter a patchy-delivery modality (EVIDENCE contradictory, PMID 40673967).

plan.critical_question: Does any nanocarrier transfect a large, deep, distributed fraction of postmitotic CNS neurons — including brainstem — after intrathecal dosing? This is a carrier-existence question, and because the answer is currently no, the MECP2-specific therapeutic hypothesis is not yet testable. Do not run a MECP2 mRNA experiment; run the gating delivery experiment, and only on a success proceed.
plan.proposed_experiment: Modality-agnostic go/no-go delivery screen, explicitly decoupled from MECP2. In wild-type mice (then, if positive, one non-human-primate confirmation because CSF geometry is the key scaling variable), dose a panel of candidate CNS-tropic LNPs and alternative nanocarriers intrathecally with a reporter mRNA encoding a nuclear-localised fluorophore. Quantify by single-cell imaging and snRNA-seq, per region (superficial cortex, deep cortex, hippocampus, striatum, brainstem respiratory nuclei): percent of NeuN-positive neurons expressing reporter, percent of glia, and per-cell expression spread (coefficient of variation) as a direct proxy for how badly an uncontrolled burst would violate a dose window. Pre-specify a pass bar before dosing (for example >=30% of neurons transfected in deep structures including brainstem, with per-cell expression spread under a defined fold-range). In parallel and at low cost, use patient iPSC-derived neurons to transfect candidate MECP2 mRNA constructs — including the untested self-limiting designs (truncated methyl-DNA-binding plus NCoR-interaction domains, destabilising UTRs/degrons; HYPOTHESIS, not_studied) — and measure per-cell MeCP2 against endogenous plus H3K9/H4K16 acetylation reversal, to learn whether per-cell output can be capped at all before any in vivo investment.
plan.model: Wild-type mouse intrathecal reporter-mRNA biodistribution screen with single-cell regional quantification (NHP confirmation only if the mouse bar is cleared); patient iPSC-derived neurons for construct-level per-cell dose-capping.
plan.primary_readout: Percent of neurons transfected in deep brain and brainstem after intrathecal dosing, plus per-cell expression spread. Secondary (in vitro): whether any construct design holds per-cell MeCP2 within ~1.5x of endogenous while reversing H3K9/H4K16 hyperacetylation.
plan.supportive_result: A carrier clears the pre-specified neuronal transfection bar in deep structures and brainstem with a narrow per-cell expression spread, AND an in vitro construct design keeps per-cell MeCP2 near endogenous while restoring the chromatin readout. Decision: the hypothesis becomes testable; only then build a MECP2 mRNA program and test it in Mecp2+/- female mice with per-cell occupancy endpoints (as specified for the protein modality).
plan.negative_result: No carrier reaches the neuronal bar in deep structures or brainstem (the expected outcome given published patchy, surface- and glia-biased intrathecal LNP distribution), or per-cell expression spread is wide, or no construct design can cap per-cell MeCP2 output. Decision: do not start an mRNA replacement program for MECP2. Redirect resources to modalities acting on the endogenous transcript or locus, which are intrinsically closer to dose-capped.
plan.decision_enabled: Whether to spend anything on MECP2 mRNA replacement now. The honest answer from current evidence is no: a program would begin with carrier invention rather than optimisation, and the modality is the worst-matched available option for a bidirectionally dose-sensitive nuclear chromatin reader. The value of the proposed experiment is that it is generic — a CNS neuronal mRNA delivery screen is reusable across many CNS indications and should not be charged to a Rett budget — while the cheap iPSC construct arm tests the one MECP2-specific question (can per-cell output be capped) for very little money. Framing it this way lets the team decline the program without foreclosing it, and revisit only if the field solves CNS neuronal mRNA delivery.
